title: Integrated Finance Playbook: Budgeting, Forecasting, Contracts, Procurement, and Revenue Recognition
author: Ava Patel
body:
Purpose
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's standard operating procedures for budgeting and forecasting, contracts and legal process, procurement, and revenue recognition and billing. It is intended for finance, legal, procurement, and business leaders (FP&A, Accounting, Legal Ops, Sales Ops, Engineering Leads) who participate in planning, committing spend, signing contracts, and recognizing revenue.

Scope
Applies to: all business units and subsidiaries, including Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private offerings.
Excludes: one-off reimbursements and personal expense items covered by the company expense policy.

Key Principles
- Financial discipline: budgets are authoritative and must be respected unless formally reforecasted.
- Single source of truth: use Redwood Finance Planning workspace (NetSuite/Adaptive integrations) for all forecasts and approved budgets.
- Risk-aware contracting: contract terms that materially change revenue recognition, data residency, or indemnity require Legal review.
- Procurement control: purchases above approval thresholds follow the procurement workflow below; preferred vendor lists must be used where available.

1) Budgeting and Forecasting
Overview
Budgeting at Redwood follows an annual top-down process combined with rolling quarterly reforecasts. The finance team publishes an annual budget calendar (owner: FP&A) and maintains a monthly forecast cadence.

Calendar and Cadence
1. Budget kickoff (Oct): leadership provides targets and headcount guidelines.
2. Department submissions (Nov): each department submits operating and capital budgets.
3. Consolidation and review (Dec): FP&A consolidates, performs sanity checks and reviews with Execs.
4. Board approval (Jan): final budget submitted for Board sign-off.
5. Rolling forecast (monthly): departments submit a 12-month rolling forecast on the 5th business day each month.

Roles and Ownership
- FP&A: publishes templates, consolidates budgets, performs variance analysis.
- Department Finance Owners (DFOs): responsible for departmental budgets and monthly reforecasts.
- People Ops: provides hiring plans and comp assumptions.
- Engineering/Product: provides project-level spend estimates for major infra and R&D initiatives.

Templates and Inputs (examples)
- Headcount template (CSV): position, level, FTE fraction, start date, comp band.
- CapEx request form: project description, business case, expected ROI, depreciation schedule.
- Run-rate report: last 12-month spend by vendor and project.

Budget Approval Matrix (summary)
| Approval Level | Max Commitment | Approver |
| Executive | > $5,000,000 | CFO + CEO |
| VP | $500,001 - $5,000,000 | VP Finance + Budget Owner |
| Director | $50,001 - $500,000 | Director + Finance Business Partner |
| Manager | $5,001 - $50,000 | Manager + DFO |
| Individual Contributor | <= $5,000 | Expense owner (with manager notice) |

2) Contracts and Legal Process
When to engage Legal
- Any contract that results in a legal obligation (e.g., Master Services Agreement, Data Processing Agreement, reseller agreements).
- Contracts with unusual indemnity, warranty, or liability clauses.
- Contract terms that impact revenue recognition (e.g., multi-element arrangements, extended payment terms).

Standard Steps (contract lifecycle)
1. Initiation: Requester completes Contract Intake Form (Confluence link and SFDC intake).
2. Triage: Legal Ops reviews intake within 2 business days and assigns a lawyer.
3. Negotiation: Counterparties provide redlines; Legal logs changes in contract tracker (owner: Legal Ops).
4. Exec Review: If contract exposure exceeds thresholds (see approval thresholds table), Legal and Finance present for Exec approval.
5. Signature: E-signature via DocuSign; executed documents stored in contract repository (GCP bucket + contract database).
6. Post-signature: Legal publishes key obligations and renewal dates to the Contracts Calendar; Finance creates accounting journal entries or revenue schedules as needed.

Contract Metadata to Capture (minimum)
- Contract ID (auto-generated)
- Parties (legal entity names)
- Effective date / Term / Renewal mechanism
- Payment terms and billing frequency
- Services and deliverables (scopes or SOWs)
- Data classification / residency clauses
- Termination rights and notice periods
- Responsible owners (Sales rep, Legal owner, Finance owner)

3) Procurement Procedures
Procurement Objectives
- Ensure cost-effectiveness and vendor security compliance.
- Centralize high-value procurement to negotiate volume discounts.
- Maintain audit trail for approvals and receipts.

Procurement Workflow
1. Determine need: Business owner identifies requirement and checks preferred vendor list.
2. Request: Submit Purchase Request (PR) via Procurement portal with business justification and budget code.
3. Sourcing: For purchase > $100k or strategic vendors, Procurement runs RFP or negotiates terms.
4. Approvals: Follow the approval matrix (Budget Approval Matrix) — system routes PR for sign-off.
5. PO issuance: Procurement issues a Purchase Order (PO) to supplier when approved.
6. Receipt & Invoice: Business confirms receipt of goods/services; Accounts Payable (AP) processes invoice against PO.

Procurement Thresholds and Routing
- <$5k: Manager approval; credit card or petty PO.
- $5k-$30k: Director approval; standard PO.
- $50k-$300k: VP approval + Procurement review.
- >$500k: Procurement + VP Finance + Legal + Exec review.

Preferred Vendor & Security Requirements
- Use vendors from the Approved Vendor Registry where possible.
- Security questionnaire (SIG or custom) required for vendors that process customer data or have network access.
- Procurement coordinates SOC2 reports, security attestations, and contracts.

Example PO table (plain-text)
| PO Field | Required? | Notes |
| vendor_name | yes | Use legal entity name |
| amount | yes | In USD unless otherwise approved |
| budget_code | yes | Department budget cost center |
| delivery_date | recommended | Expected delivery/term start |
| contract_ref | recommended | Link to contract in repository |

4) Revenue Recognition & Billing Policies
Principles
- Recognize revenue in accordance with GAAP/ASC 606: identify contract(s), performance obligations, transaction price, allocation, and recognition as obligations are satisfied.
- Finance maintains standardized revenue schedules and liaises with Legal to interpret contract terms that affect recognition.

Common Scenarios and Treatment
1. Hosted API consumption (usage-based): Recognize as revenue ratably as usage occurs if distinct service is provided and collectability is probable. Invoices monthly in arrears.
2. Dedicated capacity (committed capacity with monthly billing): Allocate transaction price between committed capacity and overage; recognize committed portion ratably over the commitment term.
3. Private deployment (license + services): If license is distinct, recognize license per license accounting; professional services recognized over time as services are delivered per SOW.
4. Multi-element arrangements: Use standard allocation policy (relative standalone selling price). Consult Controller for complex arrangements.

Billing & Invoicing Best Practices
- Standard payment terms: Net 30 unless otherwise negotiated; deviations require Finance approval.
- Invoicing cadence: monthly for consumption and recurring services; milestone invoicing acceptable for professional services with clear deliverables.
- Billing disputes: Customer must notify within 30 days of invoice date; disputes are routed to Billing Ops and Sales for resolution.

Revenue Controls and Monitoring
- Monthly close: Revenue schedules and deferred revenue reconciliations completed by the 10th business day following month-end.
- Quarterly review: FP&A and Accounting perform quarter-level revenue variance analysis and present to Execs.
- Metrics to monitor: ARR/NRR, deferred revenue balance, days sales outstanding (DSO), billing dispute backlog.

Journal & Accounting Entries (examples)
- Invoice for monthly subscription: Debit AR, Credit Revenue; if invoiced in advance, Debit Cash, Credit Deferred Revenue.
- Recognition of previously deferred revenue: Debit Deferred Revenue, Credit Revenue (as PO obligations are satisfied).

5) Controls, Auditability, and Exceptions
Documentation and Audit Trail
- All procurement requests, POs, contracts, and invoices must be retained in the central repository and linked to budget codes for audit purposes.
- Procurement and Legal Ops maintain a vendor file with SOC2, contracts, and security attestations.

Exception Handling
- Emergency spend (e.g., incident remediation) can bypass standard procurement for up to $100k with post-hoc approval by CFO + Head of Eng; requester must submit procurement intake within 3 business days.
- Any contract clause that materially changes revenue recognition or legal exposure must be escalated to Legal + Controller for an exception evaluation.

6) Operational Checklists and Playbooks
Monthly Budget Close Checklist (DFO):
- Confirm headcount changes with People Ops.
- Reconcile monthly run-rate with AP and credit card statements.
- Submit reforecast adjustments (if > 5% variance vs. budget).

Contract Close Checklist (Legal Ops):
- Contract executed and stored in repository.
- Contract metadata populated.
- Finance notified for billing setup and revenue scheduling.

Procurement Onboarding Checklist (Procurement team):
- Vendor security review complete (if required).
- PO template created and approved.
- Payment terms and tax information captured.

7) Templates and Reference Links
- Budget templates: /confluence/finance-and-legal/budgeting-and-forecasting/headcount-template.csv
- Contract intake form: /confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/contract-intake-form
- Purchase request portal: Procurement Portal (internal link)

Appendix B: Quick Decision Matrix (When to escalate)
- Any purchase > $500k: escalate to Execs & Legal.
- Contract with non-standard data residency or cross-border clauses: escalate to Legal + Security.
- Revenue deferral > $1M: Controller + CFO review required.
